simple.meaning: שָׂרַע (sâraʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to prolong , i.e. (reflex) be deformed by excess of members.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Leviticus, Isaiah, beginning at Leviticus 21:18. The surrounding contexts include offering, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׂרַע (H8311) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׂרַע (sâraʻ) / H8311 is traced through Leviticus 21:18, Leviticus 22:23, Isaiah 28:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to prolong , i.e. (reflex) be deformed by excess of members
definitions.usage: stretch out self, (have any) superfluous thing.
definitions.full: H8311. sara [ שָׂרַע ] verb extend (Arabic point directly at , also enter upon a path (Frä 213 thinks originally divide , then stretch out, make straight ), projecting roof , long-nosed ( torto naso ᵑ9 Lev 21:18 ); Ethiopic dispose, arrange ; Sabean שרע arrangement, security Hom Chr 124 ; — but Aramaic explanation as mutilated 21:18 ; 22:23 PS 2744 , compare ᵐ5 ὠτότμητος ); — Qal Passive participle שָׂרוּעַ extended , i.e. too long (in a limb or member), of man Lev 21:18 , beast 22:23 (see II. חרם ). Hithpa`el stretch oneself: Infinitive construct הִשְׂתָּרֵעַ Isa 28:20 (see מַצַּע p. 427:a). שַׂרְעַמִּים see below שׂעף .

occurrences.englishText: For whatever man he is that has a defect, he shall not draw near: a blind man, or a lame, or he who has a flat nose, or any deformity,
Either a bull or a lamb that has any deformity or lacking in his parts, that you may offer for a free will offering; but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.
